latin: Per eclipsationem solis quae accidit in morte Christi sciri potest secundum fundamenta cabalae quod tunc passus est filius dei et uerus messias.
translation: Through the eclipse of the sun that occurred at Christ's death, it can be known, according to the foundations of the Kabbalah, that then the Son of God and the true Messiah suffered.
translation_note: No technical Kabbalistic term requires gloss here; the syntax is straightforward.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-swarm-batch5, from Latin at farmer1998:27339
doctrine: Farmer's note is limited to a cross-reference: 'For the correlation between Christ and the sun, cf. 11>51' (farmer1998:27406). Thesis 11>51 states, in Farmer's cross-reference text, that as the moon was full in Solomon, so the sun was full in the true Messiah, Jesus, and that a corresponding waning can be conjectured in Zedekiah for one who searches deeply in the Kabbalah (farmer1998:27445). The thesis immediately follows 10>10, on 'the fear of Isaac', and precedes 11>47, on Satan's temptation of Christ via 'the property of Aquilo' in the Kabbalah (farmer1998:25782, 27343).
context: The 'Erkenntnistheorie und christliche Kabbalah' study groups 11>46 with 8>9 and 11>38 under a heading concerning the veil of the Temple ('Zum Tempelvorhang'), citing Pompeo Faracovi's discussion of 'il tema dell'eclissi' (the theme of the eclipse) for further background (kabbalah_paradigma:2122).
historiography: Akopyan (2018) quotes the thesis, numbered 46 in his citation of the Conclusiones Cabalisticae, immediately after quoting thesis 51 (his no. 51) on the full moon and full sun, and appends a reference to 'Secret, I cabbalisti cristiani, 60, 77-78, 137-39' for further study of the idea (akopyan2018:690). Akopyan (2021) reprints the same pairing of theses 46 and 51 in identical Latin (akopyan2021:1404). Busi and Ebgi print the thesis as their no. [93], immediately followed by 11>51 as [94], without further discursive comment in the material consulted (busi2014:25054).

quotations.text: Per eclipsationem solis quae accidit in morte Christi sciri potest secundum fundamenta cabalae quod tunc passus est filius dei et uerus messias.

not_established: The surrounding argument in Akopyan's study — what he draws from pairing theses 46 and 51 about Pico's astrologically inflected Kabbalah — is not preserved beyond the two quoted Latin theses and the bibliographic note in the material consulted (akopyan2018:690).
Faracovi's discussion of the eclipse theme, cited only at second hand (kabbalah_paradigma:2122), was not opened directly.
